items.prompt: In a tug of war, both teams pull on the rope with a force of 400 N. What happens to the rope?

options.text: It moves towards the team on the left.
options.why: Both teams pull equally hard, so neither side wins.

options.text: It does not move, because the forces are balanced.
It moves upwards.
options.why: Both forces are sideways and equal, so the rope stays still.

options.text: It speeds up towards the team on the right.
options.why: Neither force is bigger, so the rope does not start to move.

hints: Compare the size of the two forces.
The two forces pull in opposite directions.
Ask what happens when two equal forces pull in opposite directions.
items.explanation: The two teams pull with equal forces in opposite directions, so the forces are balanced. The rope does not move.

items.prompt: When the forces on an object are equal in size and act in opposite directions, the forces are ___.
hints: Think about a seesaw with the same weight on each side.
Equal and opposite forces cancel each other out.
The word starts with the letter b.
items.explanation: Equal forces acting in opposite directions are balanced. Balanced forces do not change how an object moves.

items.prompt: Team A pulls a rope to the left with 500 N. Team B pulls it to the right with 350 N. What is the size of the resultant force?
hints: The two forces pull in opposite directions.
When forces are opposite, find the difference between them.
Subtract the smaller force from the larger force.
items.explanation: The forces are opposite, so the resultant force is 500 N − 350 N = 150 N. The rope moves towards Team A, which pulls harder.

items.prompt: A boat floats without moving on a calm lake. Which two forces are balanced?

options.text: air resistance and friction
options.why: The boat is not moving, so these forces are not acting much.

options.text: gravity and magnetism
options.why: Magnetism is not acting on the boat.

options.text: the push of the wind and upthrust
options.why: Wind pushes sideways and upthrust pushes up. Balanced forces act in opposite directions.

options.text: the boat's weight pulling down and upthrust from the water pushing up

hints: The boat is not moving up or down.
One force pulls the boat down. Another force pushes it up.
Name the force that pulls everything down, then the force that water pushes up with.
items.explanation: Gravity pulls the boat down with its weight, and the water pushes it up with an equal upthrust. These forces are balanced, so the boat floats without sinking or rising.

items.prompt: Sort these into balanced forces and unbalanced forces.

items.text: a book lying still on a shelf
a car going straight at a steady speed
a lamp hanging still from a ceiling
a parachutist falling at a steady speed
a car speeding up from traffic lights

hints: Balanced forces mean no change: still things stay still, and moving things keep the same speed and direction.
Unbalanced forces change an object's speed or its direction.
For each one, ask whether its speed or direction is changing.
items.explanation: Objects that stay still, or move at a steady speed in a straight line, have balanced forces. Speeding up, slowing down or changing direction, like a bus turning, needs unbalanced forces.

items.prompt: A shopping trolley is already moving. The push forwards is 30 N and friction backwards is 30 N. What happens to the trolley?

options.text: It slows down and stops.
options.why: The forces are balanced, so nothing changes its speed. It would slow down only if friction were bigger.

options.text: It speeds up.
options.why: It would speed up only if the push were bigger than friction.

options.text: It keeps moving at the same speed.
It moves backwards.
options.why: Neither force is bigger, so its direction does not change.

hints: Compare the forward force with the backward force.
Balanced forces do not change how an object is already moving.
Decide whether the forces are balanced. Then think about the trolley's speed.
items.explanation: The forces are balanced, so there is no resultant force to change the trolley's motion. It keeps moving at the same speed in the same direction.

items.prompt: A toy car is being pushed along the floor. Which change would make it speed up?

options.text: Push harder, so the push is bigger than friction.
Push with less force than friction.
options.why: Then friction would be bigger, so the car would slow down.

options.text: Make the push exactly equal to friction.
options.why: Balanced forces keep the speed the same.

options.text: Put the car on a rougher floor.
options.why: A rougher floor gives more friction, which slows the car down.

hints: To speed up, there must be an unbalanced force forwards.
Compare the push forwards with the friction backwards.
Ask which choice makes the forward force the biggest.
items.explanation: If the push is bigger than friction, the forces are unbalanced in the forward direction. An unbalanced force forwards makes the car speed up.

items.prompt: A box is pushed to the right with a force of 20 N. Friction acts on it with a force of 5 N. Draw the box with labelled force arrows, and say what happens to it.

criteria.label: Draws an arrow pointing right, labelled 20 N
Draws an arrow pointing left, labelled 5 N
Makes the 20 N arrow longer than the 5 N arrow
Starts both arrows on the box
Says the forces are unbalanced, so the box speeds up

hints: Friction always acts against the direction of movement.
A bigger force gets a longer arrow.
items.explanation: The 20 N push to the right is bigger than the 5 N friction to the left. The forces are unbalanced, with a resultant of 15 N to the right, so the box speeds up.

items.prompt: A ball is thrown straight up. At the very top, it stops for a moment. Which force acts on it at that moment?

options.text: no force at all
options.why: Gravity never switches off. That is why the ball falls back down.

options.text: gravity, pulling it down
an upward force left over from the throw
options.why: The push from the hand stops as soon as the ball leaves it.

options.text: balanced forces holding it still
options.why: If the forces were balanced, the ball would stay at the top.

hints: The ball stops for only an instant, then falls back down.
Think about which force acts on everything near the Earth all the time.
Ask whether the hand can still push the ball once it has let go.
items.explanation: At the top, the ball is not moving, so there is no air resistance, and only gravity acts on it. This unbalanced pull makes the ball fall straight back down.

items.prompt: Three forces pull on a crate: 40 N to the right, and 25 N and 10 N to the left. What is the size of the resultant force?
hints: Forces in the same direction add together.
Add up the forces to the left, then compare the total with the force to the right.
Start by adding the two forces that pull to the left.
items.explanation: The forces to the left add up to 25 N + 10 N = 35 N. The resultant force is 40 N − 35 N = 5 N to the right, so the crate speeds up to the right.

solution.say: Add the two forces that pull to the left.
Compare the left total with the force to the right, and find the difference.
The bigger force is to the right, so the resultant is 5 N to the right.

items.prompt: Rangga runs 120 m in 20 seconds at a steady pace. What is his speed in metres per second?
hints: Speed tells you how far something goes in one unit of time.
Use speed = distance divided by time.
Divide 120 by 20.
items.explanation: Speed = distance ÷ time = 120 m ÷ 20 s = 6 m/s.

items.prompt: A cyclist rides at a steady 4 m/s for 15 seconds. How far does she go?
hints: The speed tells you the distance in each second.
Use distance = speed × time.
Multiply 4 by 15.
items.explanation: Distance = speed × time = 4 m/s × 15 s = 60 m.

items.prompt: A toy boat moves across a pond at 5 m/s. The pond is 150 m long. How many seconds does it take to cross?
hints: Think about how many 5 m steps fit in 150 m.
Use time = distance divided by speed.
Divide 150 by 5.
items.explanation: Time = distance ÷ speed = 150 m ÷ 5 m/s = 30 s.

items.prompt: A bus travels 90 km in 1.5 hours. What is its average speed in kilometres per hour?
hints: Average speed is the total distance divided by the total time.
Be careful: the time is not a whole number of hours.
Work out how far the bus goes in 1 hour: divide 90 by 1.5.
items.explanation: Average speed = 90 km ÷ 1.5 h = 60 km/h.

items.caption: A trolley moving at a steady speed
items.prompt: Amara timed a trolley. The trolley moved at a steady speed. Complete the table.
head: Time (s)
Distance (m)
hints: Steady speed means the distance grows by the same amount each second.
Find the distance in 2 seconds, then keep adding it.
The trolley goes 12 m every 2 seconds.
items.explanation: The trolley goes 6 m every second. After 6 s it has gone 36 m and after 10 s it has gone 60 m.

items.caption: A spring being stretched
items.prompt: Hadi hung weights on a spring and measured its stretch. Complete the table.
head: Force (N)
Stretch (cm)
hints: Look for the pattern between the force and the stretch.
Each 2 N makes the spring stretch the same extra amount.
2 N stretches it 3 cm, so 6 N is three lots of 2 N.
items.explanation: Every 2 N adds 3 cm of stretch. 6 N gives 9 cm and 10 N gives 15 cm.

items.prompt: Kofi slides an ice hockey puck across very smooth, slippery ice. Friction is almost zero. After one push, what will the puck do?

options.text: Slow down at once, because there is no force pushing it.
options.why: Without friction nothing slows it down.

options.text: Keep moving in a straight line at nearly the same speed.
Speed up, because nothing is stopping it.
options.why: A moving object only speeds up if there is an unbalanced force in its direction of motion.

options.text: Stop after a short time, because the push gets used up.
options.why: A push is not stored inside the puck and used up.

hints: Objects slow down because of a force, not because time passes.
What force normally slows things down?
If the forces on the puck are balanced, what does it do?
items.explanation: With almost no friction there is no unbalanced force. A moving object keeps going at the same speed in a straight line.

items.prompt: A skydiver opens her parachute and slows down. Which statement explains this?

options.text: Gravity gets weaker when the parachute opens.
options.why: Gravity stays the same. Another force changes.

options.text: Her weight has become smaller.
options.why: The parachute does not change her weight.

options.text: The air resistance pushing up becomes larger than her weight, so the forces are unbalanced upwards.
The parachute pulls her up like a rope.
options.why: Nothing is pulling her up. The air is pushing against the parachute.

hints: Slowing down means the forces are unbalanced.
Which force is made bigger by a large parachute?
Compare the upward force with the downward force.
items.explanation: The large parachute catches a lot of air, so air resistance pushing upwards becomes bigger than the weight. The skydiver slows down until the forces balance again.

items.prompt: A crate is dragged to the right at a steady speed. Tap the arrow that shows the friction force.

figure.alt: A crate on a floor with three arrows. One arrow points right from the crate, one points left from the crate, and one points straight down from the middle of the crate.

hints: Friction acts against the way the object moves.
The crate moves to the right.
Find the arrow that points the opposite way to the movement.
items.explanation: Friction opposes motion. The crate moves right, so friction acts to the left.

items.prompt: Label the parts of this picture of a skydiver.

figure.alt: A person hangs below a wide dome shape on strings. A long arrow points up on the right side of the person. Another arrow points down on the left side.

hints: Tap a label, then tap its number.
Air resistance pushes against the parachute, upwards.
The downward arrow shows the pull of gravity.
items.explanation: The wide dome is the parachute. The upward arrow is air resistance and the downward arrow is the skydiver's weight.

items.prompt: Choose 2 forces that can act on an object without touching it.

options.text: friction
gravity
magnetic force
air resistance

hints: Some forces need contact between two surfaces.
Think of a magnet pulling a paperclip from a distance.
Friction and air resistance both need touching.
items.explanation: Gravity and magnetic force act at a distance. Friction and air resistance only act when things touch.

items.prompt: Put these moving things in order, from the slowest to the fastest.
hints: Work out the speed of each one.
Divide each distance by its time.
A is 2 m/s. Now find the others.
items.explanation: A is 2 m/s, B is 4 m/s, C is 6 m/s and D is 7 m/s.

items.prompt: Match each force to an example.
pairs: An apple falls from a tree
A wooden block floats on water
hints: Think about which force is acting in each picture.
Upthrust pushes up from water.
Gravity always pulls objects down.
items.explanation: Brakes use friction, falling is caused by gravity, floating needs upthrust and a feather is slowed by air resistance.

items.prompt: When the forces on an object are ___, the object can change its speed, its ___ or its shape.
hints: Balanced forces do not change how something moves.
What kind of forces cause a change?
A moving ball can change in speed, or turn to go another way.
items.explanation: Unbalanced forces change the motion of an object. It can speed up, slow down or change direction.

items.prompt: The table shows the distance of a rolling ball from its start. What does it tell you about the forces on the ball?

options.text: The forces are unbalanced, because the ball is moving.
options.why: Moving does not mean unbalanced. Look at how the speed changes.

options.text: The forces are balanced, because the ball moves the same distance each second.
There are no forces at all on the ball.
options.why: Gravity and the ground's push still act. They are just balanced.

options.text: The forces are unbalanced, because the ball is speeding up.
options.why: The distance per second is steady, so the speed is not changing.

hints: Work out how far the ball moves in each second.
If the distance each second is the same, the speed is steady.
Steady speed in a straight line means what for the forces?
items.explanation: The ball moves 3 m every second, so its speed is steady. A steady speed in a straight line means the forces are balanced.

head: Time (s)
Distance (m)
figure.alt: A table of time and distance for a ball. The distance goes 0, 3, 6, 9, 12 metres at 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 seconds.

items.prompt: A lorry's engine pushes it forward with 900 N. Friction is 350 N and air resistance is 250 N, both backwards. What is the resultant force forwards, in newtons?
hints: Add the forces that act in the same direction first.
Add the two backward forces, then take them away from the forward force.
350 + 250 gives the total backward force.
items.explanation: Backward forces total 350 + 250 = 600 N. The resultant is 900 − 600 = 300 N forwards.

items.prompt: Citra rolls the same toy car down a ramp onto four different surfaces and measures how far it goes. Which surface has the most friction?

options.text: Carpet
Smooth tiles
options.why: The car goes furthest on tiles, so there is little friction there.

options.text: Wooden floor
options.why: The car goes further on wood than on carpet, so wood has less friction.

options.text: Rubber mat
options.why: The car stops sooner on carpet than on the rubber mat.

hints: More friction stops the car sooner.
Look for the surface where the car travels the shortest distance.
Compare the numbers in the table.
items.explanation: The car travels the shortest distance on carpet, so carpet exerts the biggest friction force.

head: Surface
Distance (cm)
figure.alt: A table showing how far a toy car rolled: smooth tiles 210 cm, wooden floor 160 cm, rubber mat 95 cm and carpet 60 cm.

items.prompt: An astronaut has a mass of 60 kg on Earth. On the Moon, gravity is weaker. Which statement is correct on the Moon?

options.text: Her mass and her weight are both smaller.
options.why: Mass is the amount of matter. It does not change.

options.text: Her mass is still 60 kg, but her weight is smaller.
Her mass is smaller but her weight is the same.
options.why: Her weight depends on gravity, so it changes.

options.text: Her mass and weight are both the same.
options.why: Weight is a force. It depends on the pull of gravity.

hints: Mass is how much matter there is. Weight is a force.
Which of the two depends on how strong gravity is?
The astronaut is made of the same stuff on the Moon.
items.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter and does not change. Weight is the pull of gravity on that mass, so it is smaller on the Moon.

items.prompt: Forces are measured in a unit called the ___.
hints: A newtonmeter is used to measure forces.
The unit is named after a famous scientist who studied gravity.
One of these is about the weight of a small apple.
items.explanation: Forces are measured in newtons (N).

items.prompt: Sort each example by what is happening to its speed.

items.text: Car cruising at 80 km/h, straight road
A ball rolling to a stop on grass

hints: Steady speed means the forces are balanced.
Ask whether the push or the resisting force is bigger.
A skydiver changes at different stages of a jump.
items.explanation: Speeding up needs a bigger forward force. Slowing down needs a bigger backward force. Steady speed means balanced forces.

items.prompt: True or false: Balanced forces on an object mean that it does not change its movement.

options.text: True
False

hints: Do forces cancel?
What happens to speed?
No change.
items.explanation: A still object stays still, and a moving object keeps the same speed in a straight line.

items.prompt: True or false: When forces are unbalanced, an object stays still.

options.text: True
False

hints: Do the forces cancel?
Which force is bigger?
It will move or change.
items.explanation: Unbalanced forces make the object speed up, slow down or change direction.

items.prompt: True or false: A book resting on a table has balanced forces acting on it.

options.text: True
False

hints: What holds it up?
Do the forces match?
They are equal and opposite.
items.explanation: Gravity pulls it down and the table pushes up with an equal force, so the book stays still.

items.prompt: True or false: A car moving at a steady speed in a straight line must have unbalanced forces.

options.text: True
False

hints: Is speed changing?
What do balanced forces do?
Balanced forces keep it steady.
items.explanation: Steady speed means balanced forces. The driving force equals the resistive forces.
